recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-34422 unless a future PA or cross-work-group decision changes how AppointmentResponse invalidation should be represented.
issue_request: FHIR-34422 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It reported that AppointmentResponse lifecycle error-handling text referred to .participantStatus=entered-in-error even though AppointmentResponse.participantStatus did not allow that code. The approved resolution was to bind participantStatus to a new ValueSet including the participation status code system plus appointmentstatus#entered-in-error, add workflow note text explaining that invalidating an AppointmentResponse uses entered-in-error or deletion, and update the modifier reason.
initial_application: Git commit 60d4ff6cd027bde1e3611af6543316027fc7c767, "FHIR-34422 Appointment Response status include entered-in-error", applied the issue by adding source/appointmentresponse/valueset-participationstatus.xml, registering appointmentresponse-status in source/fhir.ini, rebinding AppointmentResponse.participantStatus to that ValueSet, adding entered-in-error to the element short text, replacing the placeholder modifier reason with the approved reason, and adding the requested workflow note.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists appointmentresponse as a resource and appointmentresponse-status as a ValueSet source. PA minutes record a July 2022 options discussion, a September 2022 proposal review, and a September WGM 10-0-0 persuasive vote. FHIR-32165 was the broader lifecycle issue that split out the AppointmentResponse-specific concern into FHIR-34422. The only discovered Zulip hit was an implementation thread about registering the new ValueSet/OID, not a conflicting substantive decision. Later source history and the latest combined branch preserve the relevant AppointmentResponse binding, ValueSet composition, workflow note, and modifier reason.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope AppointmentResponse StructureDefinition binds participantStatus to ValueSet/appointmentresponse-status, the active ValueSet composes participationstatus plus appointmentstatus#entered-in-error, the AppointmentResponse introduction contains the invalidation note, and fhir.ini registers the ValueSet.

related_jiras.note: The lifecycle entered-in-error issue identified the AppointmentResponse mismatch and explicitly created FHIR-34422 for the resource-specific fix; it was not separately decided in this reconciliation.
